sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques; the assignment distribution is the sole stochastic design object.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, partition, graph, exposure map, and all exposure-indexed potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive categorical events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\), and the block categories are independent across \(l\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary across blocks and may vanish along triangular arrays; no uniform lower bound on \(q_l\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated.  A unanimous block reveals exactly its corresponding fixed block mean; a trimmed-out block is covered by the deterministic bounded-outcome contrast allowance.
sampling_model.randomness: The only inferential randomness is \(Z\), augmented by independent \(R\) solely to include externally randomized interval procedures in the decision class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Exposure-weighted estimators are unbiased, conservative randomization variances are available, and local-dependence conditions justify asymptotic normal intervals.

Section 4.3 constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design.

Exact confidence sets for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and stratified partial interference are obtained by inversion of randomization tests, with a targeted approximation algorithm.
Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities can be exponentially small in degree and graph-cluster randomization can sharply reduce Horvitz--Thompson variance.
Conflict-graph connectivity controls upper and lower minimax mean-squared-error rates when the design and estimator are decision variables.
Under ordinary randomized experiments, nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals attain the effective sample size \(n\pi\), with matching estimation-rate lower bounds.
Between-class moduli lower-bound expected confidence-interval length and ordered moduli yield procedures within constant factors in Gaussian models.
Convex regression classes admit finite-sample modulus-based optimal intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Under interference, existence of unbiased estimators does not guarantee variance that decreases with population size.
Randomized fuzzy intervals attain a minimum expected-length benchmark for a one-parameter Bernoulli observation problem.

body.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood All Treat and All Control exposures into independent nonidentical categorical reveals.  Exact enumeration sharpens each centered block Horvitz--Thompson increment to \(w_l/(2q_l)\), giving a clipped honest Bernstein interval with half-width \(\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+(M/6)\log(2/\alpha)\).  The capped water-filling optimizer is explicit, and the strengthened dual bounds are \(\omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le(5/2)\omega_\alpha\) and \(\omega_1\le\rho_0\le2\omega_1\), hence \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\).  A cubic lower bound valid for every measurable externally randomized interval proves the exact fixed-confidence consistency boundary \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\omega_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\rho_0\to0\).  A separate product-Rademacher anti-concentration argument gives the matching \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) rate for the designated two-scale family only.  The sole unresolved sharp-frontier claim is a universal linear lower bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\).  The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic rejects nonclique neighborhoods and otherwise compares package labels with independently recomputed unanimous-block labels before returning any interval.

project_justification.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, constructs Hoeffding intervals for binary allocation-strategy effects under two-stage Type-A partial interference, and RigdonHudgens2015 constructs exact confidence sets for those binary two-stage effects.  Neither treats the unequal-clique Bernoulli All Treat versus All Control minimax expected-length problem or proves its open universal linear water-filling lower frontier.  The exact consistency boundary is no longer a gap.
project_justification.niche: The design is the sole source of randomness, and the note separates two computable precision descriptions: the untrimmed Bernstein scales \(S\) and \(M\), and the dominance-aware capped or trimmed moduli \(\omega_\alpha\), \(\rho_\alpha\), and \(\rho_0\).  The capped modulus is necessary and sufficient for consistency even when \(S\not\to0\); its universal sharp linear finite-confidence lower interpretation remains open.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution consists of the exact categorical block reduction with centered increment \(w_l/(2q_l)\), the observed-data clipped Horvitz--Thompson interval, bias-protected trimming, the KKT-certified water-filling optimizer, the bounds \(\omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le(5/2)\omega_\alpha\) and \(\omega_1\le\rho_0\le2\omega_1\), the unrestricted upper bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\), and a cubic lower bound covering all measurable externally randomized intervals.  These results prove the full consistency equivalence.  A product-Rademacher argument additionally closes the \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) rate for the stated two-scale family, without being promoted to a universal converse.

body.technical_internal_limitation: For arbitrary heterogeneous arrays, the common-location no-reveal construction yields only \(\mathcal R_\alpha\ge\omega_\alpha^3/(128\log(1/\alpha)+8\omega_\alpha^2)\).  This is sufficient for the exact fixed-confidence consistency equivalence but may be much smaller than \(\omega_\alpha\).  The remaining sharp problem is therefore solely a universal linear weighted-erasure interval-spread converse, in both its capped global and no-dominance formulations.  A solution must control heterogeneous posterior or concentration-function spread, compact-support or moving-support boundaries, random revealed information, and independent external interval randomization.  The special product-Rademacher proof for the two-scale array does not supply this uniform step.
body.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed potential outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment.  The interval is a measurable function of \(D\) and known design quantities; its sharpened Bernstein term is \((M/6)\log(2/\alpha)\).  The KKT optimizer, trimming comparisons, cubic lower bound, and exact consistency boundary allow arbitrary independent external randomization of the reported interval.  The \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) two-sided rate is asserted only for the specified two-scale family.  No universal sharp linear expected-length lower bound is claimed.  The software diagnostic rejects overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods, and on a clique input it withholds the interval unless package labels equal the independently recomputed target exposure labels.
body.interpretation: The computable quantity \(\rho_0(w,q)\), equivalently \(\omega_1(w,q)\) up to the proved factor two, is the exact consistency diagnostic.  A rare block can keep \(S\) bounded away from zero while carrying so little causal weight that trimming it permits vanishing honest length.  At nonzero confidence the capped program supplies a certified upper modulus within factor five for expected length, and its uncapped regime reduces exactly to \(\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).  The cubic converse rules out consistency whenever the capped modulus fails to vanish.  The matching linear lower rate is known here only for the designated two-scale family, not uniformly over heterogeneous arrays.
